title: The Zen of Compensation: Paying People the Type I Way
coreMove: Take money off the table by making pay fair, sufficient, and low-drama so autonomy, mastery, and purpose can breathe.

exampleSpecs.audience: Lin, an HR lead finding the pay issue before the purpose issue
exampleSpecs.stakes: A salary meeting risks discussing engagement while people are focused on fairness.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Show pay fairness as a precondition.

exampleSpecs.audience: Gareth, a founder using pay as a trust signal
exampleSpecs.stakes: A startup offer can invite commitment or teach bargain hunting.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Use gift exchange without turning it into manipulation.

exampleSpecs.audience: Uma, a department head spotting corrosive comparison
exampleSpecs.stakes: An equity review reveals that people are tracking pay more than the work.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Show internal fairness drawing attention back to money.

exampleSpecs.audience: Cedric, a sales leader simplifying a bonus system
exampleSpecs.stakes: A bonus design rewards narrow transactions at the expense of customer value.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Show Red Gate's commission lesson in a redesign.

exampleSpecs.audience: Anika, a manager hearing pay beneath a retention story
exampleSpecs.stakes: An exit-risk conversation is being framed as lack of purpose.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Show a pay problem being named before purpose language.

exampleSpecs.audience: Rhea, a board member reducing incentive noise
exampleSpecs.stakes: A compensation committee must decide whether another metric will help or distract.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Show simpler pay supporting deeper motivation.
